sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever felt like your code is one big, messy blob? Let's fix that! Modularizing code is like organizing your closet - it makes everything easier to find and reuse.

• How to break big problems into small, manageable pieces
• Why methods are your new best friends
• How to write code that's easy to read and maintain

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine you're building a LEGO castle. Would you try to build it all in one giant piece? No way! You'd build small sections (walls, towers, gates) and then snap them together.

Modularizing code works the same way:

• **Methods** are like LEGO pieces - small, reusable blocks
• Each method does **one specific job** (like calculating tax or printing a receipt)
• You can **reuse** methods anywhere in your program

For example, instead of writing the same code to calculate square roots in 10 places, you write it **once** as a method and call it whenever needed. Cleaner, smarter, and way less typing!

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: Modularizing code means dividing a program into separate, focused methods
Each method should perform one well-defined task
Top-down design breaks a problem into subproblems, each solved by a method
Modular code is easier to read, test, debug, and maintain
Avoid duplicating code; extract repeated logic into a shared method

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Modularizing = breaking code into small, focused methods. Each method should do ONE thing well. Methods make code reusable and easier to maintain. Practice by refactoring big methods into smaller ones.

questions.question: What does 'modularizing code' mean?
options: Writing code in one long main method
Breaking code into smaller, reusable methods with specific tasks
questions.explanation: Modularizing code means dividing a program into smaller, manageable methods, each responsible for a specific task. This improves readability, reusability, and maintainability.

questions.question: What is 'stepwise refinement' in programming?
options: Breaking a large problem into smaller sub-problems solved by individual methods
Running code one line at a time
questions.explanation: Stepwise refinement is a top-down approach where a large problem is broken down into smaller, manageable sub-problems, each implemented as a separate method.
